overall_reason: The visitor mode is Persuade (a SaaS landing page for team operations); most claims are checkable and honestly worded (linked G2, Capterra, Crunchbase and AlternativeTo listings, '99.9% monthly uptime target', a named SSO and SCIM feature list), but the hero product picture is labelled both 'LIVE IN APP · Synced just now' and 'PRODUCT PREVIEW · SAMPLE DATA'; the sweep's INT-002 'Acme' hits sit inside that labelled mock and are sample data, not proof (C22); the 'Made with Lovable' tile is an honest builder mark (INT-129).

score.reason: T-PROOF-SOURCE passes for the linked directory listings and T-FIGURE-AUDIT passes for the uptime target, but T-STAGED-UI finds the hero mock claiming to be live while labelled as sample data (INT-013, Reflex), and the sweep's two INT-002 Reflex hits on 'Acme Studio' stand.

findings.where: hero product picture (div.landing-workspace-preview), sidebar foot and bottom caption, 1440 and 375; tiles/1440-00.png
findings.evidence: The hero mock shows the workspace 'Acme Studio', 'Good morning, Otto', 'Attendance 92%, 32 of 35 present' and '18 tasks due across 6 projects'. Its sidebar foot reads 'LIVE IN APP' with a green dot and 'Synced just now'. The same mock's bottom caption reads 'PRODUCT PREVIEW · SAMPLE DATA' (claims table leakage rows, pattern self-label, mock_hint). The sweep's default_names check fails 'Acme Studio' twice (INT-002). The panel tells the visitor both that it is live and that it is sample data. C22 allows sample data inside a mock but not a self-label; draft INT-134 names the label.
findings.before: "LIVE IN APP · Synced just now" and "PRODUCT PREVIEW · SAMPLE DATA" on the same picture
findings.after: Remove 'LIVE IN APP · Synced just now' from the mock and replace 'Acme Studio' with a neutral sample workspace name, so the picture reads as an illustration without needing a caption.
findings.why: The 'live' label asks the visitor to read the 92% attendance and task counts as a working product's state; the caption then admits they are invented, which weakens trust in the real claims further down.

strengths: The 'Featured on' row links each listing (G2 'Peer reviews', Capterra, Crunchbase, AlternativeTo, Software Advice), so a visitor can check every one.
The uptime figure is worded as a target ('99.9% MONTHLY UPTIME TARGET'), not as a measured result, and a 'Live Status Page' link sits in the security grid.
The security claims name their mechanisms (SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM 2.0, TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, a public sub-processor registry) instead of a bare badge.
The free plan is stated plainly and the same way each time: 'Free for up to 5 people', 'Free Starter plan for up to 5 people'.
The capture shows no countdowns, stock counts or pre-ticked boxes.
not_investigated: authenticity against outside sources: the lens does not browse, so any claim only the web could settle is not verified
checkout, signup and cancellation flows beyond the captured page
countdown or counter behaviour on reload: the capture does not reload to compare

the page's meta description says 'Start free for 14 days — no credit card', while the page itself offers a free Starter plan for up to 5 people; the pricing page was not captured, so the trial terms could not be checked
'27 BUILT-IN MODULES' and 'View all 24 features' may count different things; the features page was not captured
the launch-directory badges in the hidden 'Featured on' dialog (for example 'SaasHunt Top 1 Daily Winner') were offscreen and not seen on a tile
six badge favicons from gstatic were blocked in the capture: those images are not verified
T-DEFAULT-STATE: no checkbox or consent choice was captured on the page
T-DECLINE-READ: no dialog or decline option was captured
T-FAKE-SEND: no forms and no primary actions were captured (async: none found)
